properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 3 at 7:20AM EDT until September 3 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
SVRPBZ

The National Weather Service in Pittsburgh has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Allegheny County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Northwestern Westmoreland County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Southern Armstrong County in west central Pennsylvania...
Southern Butler County in west central Pennsylvania...
West Central Indiana County in west central Pennsylvania...

* Until 800 AM EDT.

* At 720 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
6 miles west of West Kittanning to over Gibsonia, or along a line
from 7 miles west of Kittanning to 7 miles northeast of McCandless
Township, moving southeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
McCandless Township, Cranberry, Vandergrift, Kittanning, Apollo,
Plum, Murrysville, Hampton Township, New Kensington, Lower Burrell,
Harrison Township, Wexford, Oakmont, Fox Chapel, Arnold, Tarentum
and Natrona Heights.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds.

Wind damage with these storms may occur before any rain or lightning.
Do not wait for the sound of thunder before taking cover. Seek
shelter immediately inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.

Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 830 AM EDT/730 AM CDT/.

* At 633 AM EDT/533 AM CDT/, severe thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts were located along a line extending from 34
nm southwest of C Tower to 19 nm southeast of Empire Mica Wreck to
25 nm south of S Tower to 38 nm south of V Tower. The severe
thunderstorms were nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots...suddenly higher
waves...frequent lightning...and heavy downpours.

vessels. Make sure all on board are in a secure location
and wearing life jackets.

* Severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:

open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...East Central Monroe County in western New York...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Irondequoit Creek and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. This will include
Ellison Park, with water levels possibly effecting Blossom Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 946 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is expected on Irondequoit Creek in the
warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Irondequoit, East Rochester, Fairport, Brighton and Penfield.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.description:

Pennsylvania...

Centre Counties.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following creek in
Pennsylvania...

Penns Creek near Penns Creek affecting Union and Snyder Counties.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Bald Eagle Creek near Beech Creek Station.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Homes in the cottage area are cutoff by
high water and directly affect homes in this area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.6
feet on 01/19/1996.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 4:21AM CDT until September 3 at 6:45AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Polk County in southeastern Texas...
Central San Jacinto County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 645 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable
especially along FM 3128 northeast of Coldspring and SH 150 west of
Shepherd.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 418 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the warned area. Between 3 and 6 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, and monitoring approaching
scattered showers. Flash Flood Guidance is very low in this area
due to previous rounds of rainfall, especially near Coldspring.
Additional rainfall this morning would likely warrant an upgrade
back to a Flash Flood Warning.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Shepherd, Coldspring and Lake Livingston State Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
